newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls for release of Palestinian journalist.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls for release of Palestinian journalist.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority should release detained Palestinian journalist Daoud Kuttab immediately, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Thursday.

"It's our understanding that Mr. Kuttab has not been charged with any infractions, and we are very concerned about the implications of his detention both for the rule of law and for freedom of the press," McCurry told reporters.
"We believe the Palestinian Authority should release him immediately," McCurry said.
Washington has raised the matter with senior members of the Palestinian Authority but not directly with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, who is travelling, McCurry said.
The State Department said the U.S. consul general in Jerusalem, Edward Abington, paid a visit on Thursday to Kuttab, who holds U.S. citizenship.
Kuttab "appears to be in good health," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
On Wednesday, Speaker of the Palestinian Legislative Council Ahmed Korei announced to legislators Kuttab's detention by police and said the council would demand an explanation.

Kuttab's brother told Reuters on Wednesday that Kuttab was summoned to Ramallah by Palestinian police. The journalist, who lives in East Jerusalem, went to the Ramallah self-rule enclave in the West Bank and was detained.

The brother said the detention was apparently related to a dispute between Kuttab, who has a private contract to carry live broadcasts of Palestinian Legislative Council sessions, and Palestinian state-run television.
